content.title: About
content.content: Apple cider is a fermented beverage made from pressed apple juice. It has a refreshing taste with a hint of sweetness and fruity acidity. Cider can be non‑alcoholic or contain a low alcohol content (usually up to 5 %).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of cider making dates back to ancient Celtic cultures.
In different countries the drink has various names: in England it’s called cider, in France cidre, and in Russia it’s often referred to as “apple cider”.
Cider can be “dry” (less sugar) or “sweet” (more residual sugar).
Old recipes sometimes included spices such as cinnamon and clove.
The United States celebrates an annual “World Apple Cider Day” dedicated to this drink.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Apple cider contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fermentation creates probiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: May lower cholesterol
items.content: Pectin found in apples can help reduce LDL (“bad”) cholesterol levels.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Cider is a fluid that provides electrolytes, aiding in maintaining proper hydration.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The fermentation process retains B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, important for metabolism.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Even low levels of alcohol may be unsuitable for children, pregnant women, and those avoiding alcohol.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet cider varieties can contain significant sugar, which is a concern for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature of the drink may cause heartburn in people sensitive to acid.

items.title: Apple allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to apples should avoid cider as it can trigger reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve apple cider chilled in glasses or mugs. It can be used as a base for cocktails, added to marinades, sauces, or desserts. In colder weather, cider is often served warm with spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cider in a cool, dark place. Once opened, seal the bottle tightly and keep it in the refrigerator, where it stays fresh for 7‑10 days. Discard if it becomes cloudy, develops sediment, or has an off‑smell.
